sampling_model.design: For each fixed even \(m\), one-record laws belong to \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\); the observed experiment is \(\mathbb P_{P,n}=\{P\circ(X,A,L)^{-1}\}^{\otimes n}\).
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent draws from the observed marginal of one fixed-\(m\) full-data law, with only \(X,A,L\) observed.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of both potential losses conditional on \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell-arm has known probability \(1/(2m)\); realized counts may be zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All \(2m\) survival tails are estimated from raw random-count samples by a total thresholded Hall procedure; no nuisance convergence rate is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation (4) supplies a marginal upper-cost-quantile decision objective and its conformal limit can become uninformative when support information is inadequate; it is a non-nested consumer anchor, not a Hall-class inclusion or a rate engine.
Theorem 1 bounds constrained-policy regret for regular mean welfare by a policy-complexity and efficient-score scale.
The paper estimates a policy maximizing a fixed marginal potential-outcome quantile and derives nonstandard fixed-level asymptotics.

Its one-tail Hall results motivate the coordinatewise benchmark after the translation \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\). Each conditional tail here is a compact translated slice of that one-tail class, but the full randomized \(2m\)-tail causal experiment is a stricter product construction and the open capacity-mixture upper bound does not follow from their theorems.
The paper develops extreme-value inference for the average distribution of predetermined heterogeneous power-law observations.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds honest scalar tail confidence length by worst-case bias and the paper constructs a bias-aware interval.
Theorems 4.3 and 5.1 give process inference for extreme treatment contrasts over tail levels and fixed treatment pairs.
The manuscript derives finite-sample minimax-regret treatment rules for a fixed quantile with outcomes restricted to the unit interval.

body.tldr: Capacity-constrained treatment choice at a beyond-sample loss quantile is governed by the inverse of a selected heterogeneous survival mixture. The proved results are a computable coordinatewise upper bound, the matching two-cell rate, and a sharper multiscale same-class lower envelope obtained from the exact distribution of missed paired heavy cells after unrestricted capacity reallocation. The exact all-sequence many-cell upper frontier and its if-and-only-if vanishing criterion remain open. The simultaneous-inference width converse and exact shrinking criterion also remain a separate open question.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-level quantile-policy methods do not address extrapolated Hall tails. One-tail Hall theory gives a coordinatewise familywise benchmark, and regular policy-learning theory gives an additive-welfare benchmark, but neither supplies the capacity-aware oracle inequality needed to decide whether the new multiscale paired-splice lower phases are attainable over the full heterogeneous product experiment.
project_justification.niche: For each fixed even cell count, randomization identifies every policy mixture and capacity optimization is computable by sorting. Heterogeneous indices, local ties, empty observed cells, and growing mixture mass remain in the model; the new lower argument handles global capacity reallocations by posterior factorization rather than by a mean Hamming bound.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the generic full-class regret sandwich, the exact two-cell frontier, and a multiscale paired-splice lower envelope with constant-information, intermediate, and familywise-testing phases. It leaves the matching full-class capacity-aware learner explicit as the remaining regret problem and keeps confidence-width optimality separate from regret.

body.related_work: CarpentierKim2015 is one-tail statistical substrate, not a capacity-policy theorem. Each conditional tail in this note is a compact translated slice of its one-tail Hall class after the parameter conversion \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\), while the full randomized causal experiment couples \(2m\) such tails through a stricter product construction. The paired-splice converse transfers upward only to an explicitly defined superclass containing every constructed full-data law; an upper bound must be rechecked on that superclass and does not transfer from the splice. AtheyWager2021 and KitagawaTetenov2018 concern regular additive welfare, so their \(\sqrt{m/n}\)-type scale is a comparator rather than a tail-regret proof. WangZhouSongSherwood2018 and XiaZhangKong2026 occupy fixed-level quantile-policy identification or learning. OsamaZachariahStoica2020 supplies the non-nested marginal upper-cost-quantile consumer objective; it is neither a class-inclusion statement nor a rate engine for this Hall experiment. Its support-based conformal limit motivates the extrapolation question but does not establish the answer. Predetermined heterogeneous-tail pooling, scalar tail intervals, and fixed-pair extreme-treatment inference likewise do not resolve selection among capacity-constrained mixtures.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The prior mean-only obstruction is resolved: conditioning on fixed-sample pair counts preserves posterior independence, concavity removes any advantage from zero/double capacity reallocations, and a binomial lower bound controls missed heavy cells from constant through order-\(\log m\) testing information. The unresolved regret step is now exclusively achievability over the full Hall class: no proved learner controls data-dependent selected tail weights at the multiscale lower envelope without reverting to the coordinatewise maximum. Consequently the exact many-cell rate, every claimed logarithmic elbow, and the if-and-only-if vanishing criterion remain open. The confidence-width converse and exact shrinking condition remain separately open as well.
body.honest_scope: Established claims are the fixed-cell Hall model and identification setup, sorting and inversion, Hall-core approximation, the local-dominance map, the generic coordinatewise regret sandwich, the two-cell matched rate, the simultaneous confidence upper system, and the new multiscale paired-splice lower envelope. The lower envelope applies to the same Hall class and all measurable randomized learners, but it is not yet a minimax equivalence. The exact many-cell capacity-aware upper frontier and the sharp confidence-width frontier remain open. No common tail index, fixed gap, density, nonempty realized cell sample, nuisance-rate assumption, or selection penalty is imposed. A paired-splice converse may be exported only to a superclass explicitly containing its full-data laws; the corresponding upper bound requires a separate proof.
